purpose: explicit, exhaustive mapping of every TotalSegmentator "total" label to one pilot tissue class, for the CT prior channels of the rgb-plus-ct-prior variant only (plan B stage 2). It never enters the loss target, the reference or the metrics: the target stays registry/cryo-tissue-map.json applied to the Denver original labels. Kept as a separate registry so the identity hashes of registry/machine-acceptance-protocol-v1.json stay valid; a change here is a new version of THIS file and of the prior volume, and invalidates any training run bound to the old hash.

prior_task.licence: Apache-2.0 weights, the only task this project ships
prior_task.input: data/derived/nlm-vhf/vhf-fresh-ct.nii.gz (NLM VHF fresh CT, this donor, female)
prior_task.note: a naming tool run on the donor's own CT; mixed-sex training data is allowed for naming under the sex rule of CLAUDE.md

classes.name: none
classes.definition: organs, vessels, nervous tissue and unlabelled CT voxels: all three prior channels are 0 there. Not background, not a negative: the prior says nothing.

encoding: three binary uint8 channels in the fixed order bone, cartilage, muscle, appended after the three RGB channels; a voxel with no mapped label is 0 in all three. No distance channel and no uncertainty channel in this pilot: a single model gives no disagreement map, and plan B section 3.2 reserves those for the three-model consensus of stage 1.

placement.type: rigid, no scale, fitted on the pelvis (CT hip bones and sacrum onto the Denver pelvis)

measured_error_by_structure_mm.kind: surface distances between the placed CT bone and the Denver mesh of the same bone, not a uniform per-voxel offset of the prior; a rigid misplacement shows up as a distance that varies over a surface

placement.limit: The pilot block is mostly thigh. Under this pelvis-fitted transform the femur surfaces sit 7.5 to 8.7 mm from the Denver femur surfaces, against 4.7 mm p95 at the pelvis; with their own rigid fits the femora reach 3.4 to 4.4 mm, and those fits are measured and applied nowhere. These are surface distances, NOT a uniform offset applied to every prior voxel, and nothing here separates segmentation difference from placement. The prior is a prior; the colour edge decides.

protocol_erratum.text: registry/machine-acceptance-protocol-v1.json says "the CT prior variant carries the fresh-CT placement error of the pelvis (3 to 5 mm) into its input channel". That figure describes the pelvis, which is where the transform was fitted, and understates this block, which is mostly thigh.
protocol_erratum.why_not_corrected_there: the protocol is frozen and its own sha256 gates the evaluator; editing it silently would void protocol v1. The erratum is recorded here and in docs/PROGRESS.md instead, and the protocol is changed only by a version 2.

limits: one model, not the three-model consensus of plan B stage 1: no disagreement map and no uncertainty channel
TotalSegmentator "total" has no thigh muscle label, so the muscle prior is empty over most of the primary slices; the measured coverage is in generated/cryo-ct-prior-block2.json
costal_cartilages is the only cartilage label and it lies above the primary slices

the fresh CT was acquired on a table and the block was frozen in another posture; above the pelvis the photograph-to-CT mapping is extrapolated, which is why the auxiliary stratum stays off under protocol v1
nothing here is anatomy: a label name from an automatic tool on one CT
